subject: Accountancy
central_question: How does a cash flow statement explain the change in cash and cash equivalents through operating, investing and financing activities?
in_scope_units: Objectives and benefits of a Cash Flow Statement.
Meaning of cash, demand deposits and cash equivalents under AS 3.
Meaning of cash flows and exclusion of movements between cash and cash equivalents.
Classification of operating, investing and financing activities.
Treatment of extraordinary items, interest, dividends, income taxes and non-cash transactions.
Ascertainment of operating cash flow by direct and indirect methods, with emphasis on the indirect method.
Adjustment of net profit for non-cash, non-operating and working-capital items.
Ascertainment of investing and financing cash flows from financial statements and additional information.
Preparation and reconciliation of the complete Cash Flow Statement.
banned_topics: Accrual-based preparation of the Statement of Profit and Loss, which belongs to Financial Statements of a Company.
Ratio-based liquidity analysis, which belongs to Accounting Ratios.
Fund-flow statements and advanced treasury forecasting not included in the chapter.
must_include_keywords: profit on sale of fixed assets

known_pitfalls.claim: Profit and cash from operating activities are always equal.
known_pitfalls.correction: Profit is accrual-based and includes non-cash and non-operating items; the indirect method adjusts it to obtain operating cash flow.

known_pitfalls.claim: Purchase of a cash equivalent is an investing cash outflow.
known_pitfalls.correction: Movements between cash and cash equivalents are part of cash management and are not treated as cash flows in the statement.

known_pitfalls.claim: An increase in trade receivables is added to operating profit.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is deducted because revenue recognised has not yet produced the corresponding cash.

known_pitfalls.claim: Conversion of debentures into shares is a financing cash inflow and outflow.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is a non-cash financing transaction and is disclosed separately rather than included in cash-flow totals.

recommended_example_progression: Use Test Your Understanding–I to classify the listed transactions as operating, investing, financing or cash equivalents.
Use the Section 6.6 example with profit before tax Rs. 30,000 to learn indirect-method adjustments.
Use the working-capital rules and Test Your Understanding–II to practise plus, minus and no-change effects.
Use the fixed-asset-account illustrations to derive purchases and sale proceeds for investing activities.
Use NCERT Illustrations 7–10 to prepare complete direct or indirect Cash Flow Statements.
Use Numerical Questions 11–12 to reconcile opening and closing cash and cash equivalents.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions for Practice and Numerical Questions 1–12, followed by answers to Test Your Understanding–I and II.
